fixed_product_decisions.summary: Product thesis: The Gallery is a maker-led digital gallery for art and craft objects. Makers present their own work with the dignity of an exhibition. Visitors discover the object, understand who made it, and approach the maker directly to buy, commission or learn.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: MANUAL: every stage gate compares intended journey and interface against this thesis (Audit Protocol L-A24)

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Governing distinction and line: a marketplace asks how to complete the sale; a social network asks how to keep a person scrolling; The Gallery asks how to let the work be seen and make it easy to reach the person who made it. The Gallery hosts the encounter; the maker owns the transaction.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: MANUAL: design review lens; structural promises checked by GAL-04/GAL-08/GAL-09 loci

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Work first.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: Public entrance route renders one published work at substantial scale before any feature tile; entrance render read at phone width (L-A6) plus a DOM-order assertion
fixed_product_decisions.required_consequence: The public entrance begins with real work, not feature tiles, promotions or creator performance.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Maker-owned presentation.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: Server-side ownership rule: only the owning maker writes presentation, order, availability and retirement of their work; cross-maker denial probe under ordinary credentials
fixed_product_decisions.required_consequence: Each maker controls the truthful presentation, order, availability and retirement of their own work.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Direct contact.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: Publish gate: a gallery advertises contact only with at least one enabled public route; contact action resolves to the exact enabled route; disabled/malformed routes never render as active
fixed_product_decisions.required_consequence: Every eligible work, commission and workshop path reaches a maker-approved external contact or registration route.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: No platform transaction.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: Route inventory and schema contain no cart/checkout/wallet/escrow/order/shipping/refund/dispute objects; banned-vocabulary sweep over source, schema and copy
fixed_product_decisions.required_consequence: No cart, checkout, wallet, escrow, order, shipping, refund or commercial-dispute workflow exists.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: No transaction cut.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: No fee, commission or revenue field is linked to any sale, commission or workshop; refusal register GAL-R03; vocabulary sweep
fixed_product_decisions.required_consequence: The Gallery receives no percentage of a private sale, commission or workshop fee.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Maker-authored claims.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: All claim fields (work, process, price, availability, practice) are writable only by the owning maker and rendered as maker-authored; no operator or system edit of claim text
fixed_product_decisions.required_consequence: Claims about work, process, price, availability and practice are supplied and maintained by the maker.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: No quality or reliability certification.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: scripts/doctrine-gate.py G5 fails any commit whose rendered copy surfaces under ux/reference/interface/surfaces/ carry the banned vocabulary; .githooks/pre-commit executes it on every commit.
fixed_product_decisions.required_consequence: The platform does not claim that work is authentic, handmade, high quality, safe to buy, or that a maker is commercially reliable.
fixed_product_decisions.scope_debt: The sweep's root set is the rendered copy surfaces that exist today. Application source and the governed copy home enter the same root set in Stage 2; carried as obligation OBL-GAL-012 with its activation condition, never as prose inside this clause (L-A19).

fixed_product_decisions.summary: No public popularity economy.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: Schema holds no public counters; no like/rating/review/comment/repost/follower-count/streak/leaderboard object or copy; vocabulary sweep
fixed_product_decisions.required_consequence: No public likes, ratings, reviews, follower counts, comments, reposts, streaks, leaderboards or popularity badges.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: No engagement-ranked feed.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: Browse ordering is a documented, deterministic function of recency, neutral rotation and explicit filters; test asserts its inputs contain no engagement signal
fixed_product_decisions.required_consequence: Discovery is understandable and may not be driven by opaque engagement optimisation.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: No paid discovery rank.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: No paid or sponsored attribute exists on any discovery input; refusal register GAL-R09
fixed_product_decisions.required_consequence: Payment may not buy ordinary discovery position or masquerade as merit.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Public value before identity.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: Anonymous probe of every public route (Browse, search, material, work, maker gallery, collection, workshop, contact handoff) returns the surface without a session
fixed_product_decisions.required_consequence: Visitors can encounter, browse and share work without an account wall.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Maker email door.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: Auth configuration allows email only; the complete door (create, confirm, sign in, non-enumerating denial, resend, reset, session persistence, expiry, sign out, resume, closure, suspension/reinstatement) walked on the deployed product with a real test email
fixed_product_decisions.required_consequence: Makers create an account and sign in through email. Phone-number and social-login doors are not part of the MVP.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Maker-led does not mean ownerless.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: Operator surface with report, takedown/restore, suspend/reinstate and category management, each recorded append-only with actor, time and reason
fixed_product_decisions.required_consequence: The platform owns reliable access, publishing, search, privacy, reporting, blocking, takedown, suspension and reinstatement.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Moderation is not curation.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: Operator actions are an enumerated set (takedown, restore, suspend, reinstate, dismiss, close, category vocabulary); no ranking, featuring-by-taste or claim-editing action exists
fixed_product_decisions.required_consequence: The operator may act on misuse, impersonation, spam and prohibited content, but does not rank or approve artistic taste.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Truth at the handoff.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: The contact handoff surface renders the governed disclosure (GAL-C1) before any external navigation; test asserts by role/test-id, never literal copy
fixed_product_decisions.required_consequence: Before leaving for direct contact, the visitor can understand that payment, delivery, returns and disputes are arranged with the maker.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: No false knowledge of private commerce.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: Schema records contact intent only; no sale, fulfilment or resolution status exists; copy sweep for claims of completed transactions
fixed_product_decisions.required_consequence: The product may record contact intent, but may not claim a sale, fulfilment or resolution it cannot observe.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Opening-screen law: the first meaningful public screen opens on one real work at substantial visual scale; the visitor is already inside The Gallery. fixed_product_decisions.summary: Working name: use The Gallery consistently as the product name and machine-readable identity (thegallery). Option A of the Stage 1 instrument, ratified.
fixed_product_decisions.question: Working name.
fixed_product_decisions.reason: The product wears the name in every surface already; leaving it a working title costs nothing now and costs a sweep of copy, routes and fixtures after launch.
fixed_product_decisions.consequence_of_rejection: Rejecting A means renaming before Stage 2 (option B) or carrying an unlocked name the product uses anyway (option C).
fixed_product_decisions.reopen_condition: A governor decision to rename, executed as a single governed sweep across copy, routes, fixtures and renders in one change.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: Every render, route, copy string and fixture carries the single name; each stage gate compares rendered copy and route inventory against it, and a rename is a governed sweep rather than an edit.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Account boundary: a maker gallery may be held by an individual maker, a studio or a collective presenting work they created or materially produced. Retailers and ordinary resellers are excluded. Option B of the Stage 1 instrument, ratified.
fixed_product_decisions.question: Account boundary: who may hold a maker gallery?
fixed_product_decisions.reason: Collective and studio craft is common in the target context, so individual-only would exclude real makers; admitting retailers and resellers would turn a gallery into a listing platform and contradict the product thesis GAL-T1.
fixed_product_decisions.consequence_of_rejection: Option A excludes collective craft; option C admits resale and changes what the product is.
fixed_product_decisions.reopen_condition: A governor decision that changes GAL-T1's thesis, since the boundary is what keeps the product a gallery rather than a marketplace.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: The domain model carries maker kind (individual, studio, collective); the published participation rules state the boundary; prohibited resale is one of the five report categories in the moderation standard, which is the post-publication path when the boundary is crossed.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Admission: open maker account creation by email, with self-declaration at gallery creation, published participation rules and post-publication moderation. There is no pre-publication taste or quality gate and no verification claim. Option A of the Stage 1 instrument, ratified.
fixed_product_decisions.question: Admission mechanism.
fixed_product_decisions.reason: A pre-publication review installs the taste gate the operator is forbidden to hold under GAL-14 and makes the founder a blocking step in every first publish. An invitation cohort can be layered on later without changing the mechanism.
fixed_product_decisions.consequence_of_rejection: Option B installs a forbidden taste gate; option C is compatible with A and needs no decision now.
fixed_product_decisions.reopen_condition: A governor decision that changes GAL-14's limit on operator authority.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: The publish path contains no operator review step; the operator's authority is the report queue, takedown, suspension and reinstatement, each with a recorded reason and an appeal route.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Launch geography: Bengaluru is used for realistic demonstration content and the first real makers, while geography stays a configurable field. The product makes no Bengaluru-only and no India-wide launch claim. Option A of the Stage 1 instrument, ratified.
fixed_product_decisions.question: Launch geography and how location shapes discovery.
fixed_product_decisions.reason: India-wide from day one dilutes the first cohort and raises the Nearby question before any location data exists; a city-locked product hard-codes a boundary the domain model would then have to enforce.
fixed_product_decisions.consequence_of_rejection: Option B dilutes the cohort; option C hard-codes a boundary that is expensive to remove.
fixed_product_decisions.reopen_condition: A governor decision to make a public geographic claim, which requires the discovery behaviour that would make the claim true.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: Location is a configurable field rather than a hard-coded boundary in the domain model; rendered copy carries no geographic launch claim, and the claim sweep over rendered surfaces is the check that holds it.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Direct contact: a maker may choose any of public WhatsApp, public email, phone, website or an external form. At least one route is required before direct contact is advertised, and not before work can be published. The private account email stays private unless separately supplied as a public route. There is no in-app chat. Option A of the Stage 1 instrument, ratified.
fixed_product_decisions.question: Contact routes: which routes, how many required, and no in-app chat.
fixed_product_decisions.reason: Requiring a route to publish at all blocks the one-sitting first publish that J-002 is built around; a platform-relayed enquiry form makes the product the intermediary and creates the moderation and privacy duty refused in GAL-R04.
fixed_product_decisions.consequence_of_rejection: Option B blocks the first publish; option C creates a duty the product has refused.
fixed_product_decisions.reopen_condition: Stage 3 evidence that external routes fail visitors, ruled by the governor, which would also reopen GAL-R04.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: The publish gate advertises contact only when at least one public route is enabled; the contact action resolves to the exact enabled route; the account email is a separate private field that no public surface reads; the route inventory contains no messaging or chat object.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Social depth: private, device-local saves only in the MVP. Public counts, comments, reactions and popularity ranking stay refused. Count-free following and low-volume notices may be reconsidered later as a separate candidate. Option A of the Stage 1 instrument, ratified.
fixed_product_decisions.question: Social depth at launch.
fixed_product_decisions.reason: Following in the MVP introduces a visitor identity, a notification substrate and a privacy surface before the core maker-to-visitor chain is proven; removing saves altogether takes away the visitor's only memory and weakens return visits.
fixed_product_decisions.consequence_of_rejection: Option B builds identity infrastructure before the core chain works; option C removes the visitor's memory.
fixed_product_decisions.reopen_condition: A separate governor candidate for count-free following and low-volume notices, which requires an optional visitor identity decision first; public counts and popularity ranking stay refused independently of it.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: Saves are held on the visitor's device with no server record and no visitor identity; no public surface renders a count, a comment, a reaction or a popularity order; the refusal register carries the standing refusals and their reopen conditions.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Identity confirmation: deferred beyond the MVP. The Gallery makes no verification claim at launch, and carries no badge and no verification vocabulary. Option A of the Stage 1 instrument, ratified.
fixed_product_decisions.question: Identity confirmation.
fixed_product_decisions.reason: A badge needs review, privacy, renewal, appeal and revocation mechanisms before it may appear; none exist, so a badge at launch would be a promise without a mechanism.
fixed_product_decisions.consequence_of_rejection: Option B requires building all five mechanisms in the MVP.
fixed_product_decisions.reopen_condition: A narrow implemented mechanism that earns the exact statement made, ruled by the governor under the constraints in GAL-RC5.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: No surface renders a verification badge or verification vocabulary; the claim sweep over rendered surfaces holds the vocabulary; the constraints recorded in GAL-RC5 bind any reopening.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Revenue: no monetisation is implemented in the MVP. The presentation architecture stays capable of supporting subscription plans later. There is no transaction percentage, no advertising and no paid ranking. Option A of the Stage 1 instrument, ratified.
fixed_product_decisions.question: Revenue and maker plan limits.
fixed_product_decisions.reason: Plans in the MVP add billing, entitlements and limit enforcement before a single maker-to-visitor chain is proven, which is the admin-before-value scar the Doctrine records.
fixed_product_decisions.consequence_of_rejection: Option B builds the billing surface first.
fixed_product_decisions.reopen_condition: A governor decision to introduce subscription plans, taken with the plan limits in the same ruling; a transaction percentage, advertising and paid ranking stay refused.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: The route inventory and schema contain no billing, entitlement, plan-limit, advertising or paid-ranking object; presentation limits are configurable values rather than plan-bound ones, so a later subscription needs no change to the presentation model.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: Moderation standard: publish a minimal standard before launch covering impersonation, prohibited or unlawful content, spam or systematic misuse, prohibited resale and safety concerns. Every sanction carries a recorded reason, is reversible where appropriate, and supports appeal by email to a published address. Moderation protects access and safety; it does not curate taste and does not certify maker claims. Option A of the Stage 1 instrument, ratified.
fixed_product_decisions.question: Moderation standard: report categories, response expectations, prohibited content, appeal and reinstatement rules.
fixed_product_decisions.reason: Without a named standard the operator's authority is unbounded and unexplained, which GAL-14 forbids; a full policy document with response-time guarantees makes promises a single founder cannot keep.
fixed_product_decisions.consequence_of_rejection: Option B leaves operator authority unbounded; option C makes unkeepable promises.
fixed_product_decisions.reopen_condition: A governor decision to widen or narrow the categories, or to convert the response-time intent into a guarantee, which requires the capacity to keep it.
fixed_product_decisions.enforcement_locus: The published standard names the five report categories and the appeal address; every sanction writes a reason and a reversal path; the operator surface offers takedown, suspension and reinstatement and offers no quality or taste judgement.

fixed_product_decisions.summary: The data and auth path return to Supabase-native: Supabase Auth owns the maker door, the application reaches its data through PostgREST with @supabase/supabase-js, and row-level security keys on auth.uid(). A token minted for either product is structurally valid at the other's API; only row-level security separates them. Accepted knowingly, alternative (a dedicated project) declined.

fixed_product_decisions.required_consequence: The eighteen-step chain walks again on the rewritten path before any claim is made about it. Until then the rewritten path is proved by nothing.

mandated_outcomes.outcome: Structural model: shared public Gallery → maker-owned gallery → individual work → maker's practice → commission or workshop invitation → direct contact handoff. The shared environment enables discovery and never displaces the maker's gallery as the place where a body of work is understood.

Visitor journey: enter without signing in; encounter work; open one work at meaningful scale; understand it through restrained factual information; move into the maker's gallery and practice; save privately, share the exact link, or choose a contact intention; see the direct-contact boundary and move to the maker's approved route. No platform checkout after contact.

Maker journey: For Makers → email account with real deployed verification → maker/studio/collective identity, location, practice note, public contact routes → gallery and first work → deliberate arrangement and optional collections → work status, commission availability, workshops → share → receive enquiries outside the platform → maintain, reorder, unpublish, retire → edit profile, recover access, sign out, close account through complete paths.

Operator journey, required before public launch and not before the first validated maker-to-visitor chain: protected door; new reports and unresolved operating failures; inspect with context; takedown/restore, suspend/reinstate, dismiss/close; record reason and outcome without rewriting history; manage the material vocabulary; identify failed publishing/contact paths.

Accessibility and professional behaviour: WCAG 2.2 AA; no low-contrast, colour-only or delicate-type dependence; active categories signalled by more than amber; labelled icons; component-level touch, focus, keyboard and screen-reader design; maker-authored alt text with an honest fallback; reduced-motion respected; every loading, empty, partial, stale, failed and denied state is a designed surface.

Technical and data integrity standard: durable deep links and truthful share previews; managed email authentication; persistent database; proper object storage with non-destructive image variants; server-side access controls; migration discipline; environment separation with no credentials in source; diagnostic logging; a deployed phone-walkable environment; no service-worker fetch cache. The twelve decisive integrity seams of §13 hold.

Professional UX completeness: the before, during, success, failure, interruption and return states of every meaningful journey are designed; the state families of §14 are represented; forms ask only for used data, explain public vs private, validate near the field, preserve input, preview before consequential publishing, prevent duplicate submission, and name consequences before destructive acts; excellent behaviour from a WhatsApp link in a mobile browser at small phone, large phone, tablet and desktop widths; observed performance, not inferred.

recommended_decisions.summary: Artist and artisan boundary without certification: maker self-declaration at gallery creation, clear participation rules, a report route for impersonation, prohibited resale or systematic misuse, operator takedown/suspension with appeal/reinstatement, and no 'verified', 'vetted', 'authentic' or 'safe' claim. No pre-publication quality or taste gate in the MVP. A stricter admission system is a governor decision.
Navigation: Browse · Saved · Workshops · For Makers, with search globally available. Fable may refine only with a shown comparison that weakens no journey (Stage 1 records the comparison).

Work commercial/display status: available · made to order · enquire · sold · on view — separate from the work lifecycle draft → published → retired; stale status is detectable and honestly labelled or prompted for reconfirmation.

Email credential flow: email plus password with email confirmation and password reset is the current recommendation; an emailed one-time code is coherent if supported well; a magic-link-only door is refused without a proven cross-device, real-mail-client round trip.

Optional paid identity confirmation is not in the MVP. If opened, it confirms only that the person or studio controlling an account matches the displayed identity; it never implies authorship of every work, quality, handmade authenticity, transaction safety or higher rank; no badge before review, privacy, renewal, appeal and revocation mechanisms exist.

Revenue direction: maker-funded presentation infrastructure (free gallery; subscription studio plan; institutional plan) — never a transaction percentage, advertising or pay-to-rank. Monetisation implementation is deferred; the presentation architecture stays subscription-ready.

Success measures: work-detail open rate; direct-contact action from eligible work or gallery; active makers with current published work; inventory freshness and status reconfirmation; return visits and private saves without public counts; workshop and commission contact intent; failed publish/contact rate; report rate and operator resolution time; first-attempt completion of the decisive maker publishing chain. Never scroll time, posts per day, reactions, follower growth or GMV.
A gallery may publish without a contact route; contact is not advertised until a route exists and Studio shows the task. GAL-03 holds because no path is offered before a route exists.
Sold and on-view works stay visible with their status; only retirement removes a work from public surfaces.
A status unconfirmed for 90 days is labelled publicly and prompts the maker to reconfirm; nothing is auto-retired.

refusal_register.refused: In-app workshop ticketing or payment.

refusal_register.reopen_condition: Governor decision changing GAL-04.

refusal_register.refused: Advertising, sponsored works in ordinary discovery, paid placement or pay-to-rank.

refusal_register.reason: No badge before review, privacy, renewal, appeal and revocation mechanisms exist (GAL-RC5).

refusal_register.reopen_condition: Governor decision after the email door is proven and evidence shows a need.
